claims.statement: Polish owners or managers must arrange annual controls covering specified exposed building elements, environmental installations, gas installations and chimneys; five-year controls add the whole building, aesthetics and electrical/lightning measurements; qualifying large objects are controlled by 31 May and 30 November; adverse events and certain resident reports trigger additional controls.

The inspection bundle spans legally distinct qualification classes: relevant construction qualifications for general controls, construction or energy-supervision qualifications for electrical/gas controls, and chimney-master or relevant construction qualifications for chimney scopes. Unauthorized or negligent technical work can attract criminal or professional liability.

For c-KOB, the owner, manager or authorized bookkeeper attaches the periodic-control protocol; GUNB interprets the corresponding entry as due promptly and no later than seven days after the control. This creates a short, responsibility-sensitive handoff between inspector and manager.

The official c-KOB is free, records controls and documents, supports multiple roles, and already provides visibility and reminders for upcoming periodic controls. It directly substitutes for a calendar, system-of-record and reminder-only product.
The 2025 amendment replaced the transition date for legacy paper building books from 31 December 2026 with 31 December 2031, reducing near-term forced-migration urgency for existing buildings.

A professional property manager's statutory domain includes financial management, safe use, ongoing administration and maintaining condition, but the concrete scope is set by the management contract. Managers also carry mandatory civil-liability insurance, including for people acting under their supervision.

A named private manager, TZO24, solicited annual and five-year inspections for about 415 Lower-Silesian objects, including about 315 housing-community buildings. It requested per-building and inspector-hour prices, paper plus PDF protocols, defect photos and recommendations, allowed monthly settlement for completed inspections, and contemplated annual or multi-year cooperation.
The TZO24 document is evidence of a dense private procurement route, not realized spend: it contains blank price fields, no award or paid invoice, and no separate software or coordination-fee line.

Poland had nearly 16 million dwellings at year-end 2024, but this is not a denominator for privately managed multi-building portfolios, eligible buildings, inspection events or routable inspection spend.

GUNB's e-CRUB exposes a location-searchable register of nearly 130,000 qualified construction specialists, used by more than 1,000 people daily; contact details are visible only when the specialist elects to publish them.

The existence of e-CRUB makes qualification verification and some direct sourcing easier, so scarce inspector discovery is not yet a defensible moat; the register does not establish inspection-specific availability, rates, travel radius, insurance or willingness to accept marketplace economics.

Przeglądy Budynku already sells inspection calendar, mobile data capture, photos, digital signatures, property hierarchy and reports. Its current building plans include a free tier up to three buildings and an annual-plan price of PLN 1,750 net per month for up to 30 buildings, equal to PLN 700 per building per year at full utilization.

Figure advertises multi-specialty, same-visit inspection delivery with PLN 2.5 million liability cover. Its general-building prices start at PLN 300 net per object for annual/half-year scopes in larger portfolios and PLN 400 for five-year scopes, versus PLN 700 and PLN 800 respectively for one or two objects.

Using Figure's larger-package asking prices, one annual plus one-fifth of a five-year general-building scope normalizes to PLN 380 per building-year; a 15% dispatch fee would yield only PLN 57 per building-year before coordination, QA, rework, insurance or acquisition costs. This excludes gas, chimney, electrical and other scopes whose portfolio prices were not established.

Mediatis already markets nationwide portfolio coverage, coordination of multiple specialist types, annual/five-year/half-year and installation controls, protocols, defect recommendations, its own inspection app, and KOB/c-KOB assistance. This closely matches the proposed managed network rather than merely the software layer.

In a housing-community case, UODO held the community to be the personal-data controller and its contracted administrator to be an Article 28 processor. A new platform acting for that manager would therefore likely be a processor or subprocessor for personal data and could not assume unrestricted reuse rights.

No sourced evidence establishes that private managers will pay a separate PLN 600-per-building recurring fee plus a 15% dispatch fee after accounting for free c-KOB and existing software/service incumbents.

No verified, scalable list of private Polish managers with portfolio size, geography and procurement authority was found; one reachable 415-object buyer does not establish channel economics or a representative distribution.
Regional accept rates, day rates, travel limits, insurance, seasonal capacity and protocol-rework rates for each required inspector specialty remain unmeasured.

No public c-KOB integration API, commercial integration terms or supported bulk-write pathway was verified in the official materials reviewed; the candidate must assume role-based/manual operation until GUNB confirms otherwise.

A nationwide dispatch promise would combine multi-specialty credential checks, travel scheduling, short c-KOB/protocol handoffs, defect escalation, rework and liability. That operating profile is unlikely to fit a solo founder's part-time schedule without a narrow region and volume cap.

At the explicit test economics below, reaching PLN 5 million founder net worth requires roughly 7,000 retained buildings and about 70 managers of 100 buildings each by year 9; neither acquisition scale nor operating capacity is evidenced.

contrary_evidence: The free official c-KOB already supplies the system of record, roles and inspection reminders.
The legacy-paper deadline is 2031, so existing portfolios do not face a near-term mandatory software migration.
Przeglądy Budynku already sells the operating-software layer and offers a free small-building tier.
Figure's published large-package prices leave little revenue for a dispatch percentage alone.
Mediatis already markets the nationwide coordinated multi-specialty service with its own app and c-KOB help.
e-CRUB makes qualification verification and some direct local sourcing publicly available.
The one private portfolio RFP has no award price or separate platform-fee line.
Data-controller and processor roles make unrestricted inspection-data reuse an invalid assumption.

economics.acquisition_route: Build a lawful list of 30 regional private managers with 100+ buildings and sell one account at a time against a de-identified due-event calendar. TZO24 proves that at least one private 415-object portfolio can issue a centralized RFP but does not prove representativeness or conversion (R03-S06). Budget 100 founder/sales/onboarding hours for each 100-building account solely as a test assumption; record contact-to-calendar, calendar-to-proposal, proposal-to-paid-pilot, cycle time and buildings authorized.
economics.capital_required_pln: Modeled pilot requirement PLN 30,000-60,000: secure document workflow and minimal software, legal and data-processing terms, insurer and technical-QA review, partner verification, and a rework/working-capital reserve. This is an inference, not a vendor quote. Keep inspectors off payroll and do not buy inspection equipment; the amount fits the founder's PLN 100,000 personal capital without relying on parents' additional capital.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not forecast, using the founder snapshot's definition: founder business equity plus personal cash and actual after-tax distributions minus liabilities, excluding the home and avoiding any double count of retained cash. Assume 100% ownership, no debt, PLN 657 revenue per building-year, PLN 282 contribution on renewals, PLN 132 on new buildings after modeled acquisition/onboarding, fixed operating cost of PLN 35k/80k/150k/200k/250k in years 1-5 and PLN 450k in year 9, and a 3.0x normalized EBITDA value excluding excess cash. Year 1: 150 new buildings, PLN 98.6k revenue and about minus PLN 15k EBITDA. Year 2: 500 total (150 renewal, 350 new), PLN 328.5k revenue and about PLN 9k EBITDA. Year 3: 1,200 total (500 renewal, 700 new), PLN 788.4k revenue and about PLN 83k EBITDA; do not leave employment unless repeatable demand, positive contribution and 12-month runway are independently met. Year 4: 2,000 total (1,200 renewal, 800 new), about PLN 244k EBITDA under the fixed-cost assumption, the earliest plausible job-exit checkpoint. Year 5: 3,000 total (2,000 renewal, 1,000 new), PLN 1.971m revenue, about PLN 446k EBITDA and PLN 1.338m indicative equity at 3x; while employed, 95% of after-tax distributable cash remains reinvested and distributions stay at or below 5%. Year 9: 7,000 total (6,000 renewal, 1,000 new), PLN 4.599m revenue, about PLN 1.374m EBITDA and PLN 4.122m equity; only if cumulative actual after-tax distributions after an objective job exit reach about PLN 0.90m and liabilities remain zero does founder net worth reach about PLN 5.02m. This requires about 70 managers of 100 buildings, or roughly 17 portfolios the size of TZO24's solicitation, and about 8,400 annualized general-inspection scopes; none of that acquisition or operating scale is evidenced.
economics.founder_time: Pilot ceiling 15-20 hours per week, one region, no more than about 100 buildings and two or three partner firms while employed. Measure coordination and QA time per building and peak-week load. Above roughly 300 buildings or with national travel, an operations hire is assumed necessary; the May and November large-building deadlines and three-day/seven-day event/document windows make uninterrupted part-time coverage a material risk (R03-S01, R03-S04).
economics.gross_margin_basis: Explicit inference, not observed economics: PLN 657 revenue less two hours of human coordination, QA and support at PLN 150/hour (PLN 300) and PLN 75 for software, security, payments, insurance/rework allocation leaves PLN 282 steady contribution, or 43%. Assume another 100 founder/sales/onboarding hours per first 100-building account at PLN 150/hour, equal to PLN 150 CAC per new building; first-year contribution becomes PLN 132, or 20%. Any lower recurring fee, more than two hours of work, or material rework collapses the model; dispatch-only revenue of PLN 57 is insufficient.
economics.payback: At PLN 657 incremental annual cost, a buyer valuing administrative time at the modeled PLN 100/hour must save at least 6.57 paid manager hours per building-year, or receive equivalent documented procurement/rework/risk reduction. Mandatory inspection spend itself is not payback because the inspections would be bought anyway. Under the modeled PLN 150 CAC and PLN 282 renewal contribution, seller CAC payback is about 6.4 months only after the steady workload is proven; first-year cash payback remains unverified.
economics.pricing: Validation hypothesis: PLN 600 net per building-year plus a disclosed 15% fee on routed inspector invoices, with inspectors paid directly and no remediation margin. R03-S10's larger-package asking prices normalize the core general-building scope to PLN 380 per year (PLN 300 annual + PLN 400/5), hence only PLN 57 dispatch revenue and PLN 657 modeled total revenue per building-year. R03-S09's annual 30-building plan is an asking-price comparison of PLN 700 per building-year at full utilization, not proof of willingness to pay.
economics.retention_or_repeat: The legal schedule recurs annually, every five years and on events, but recurring workflow does not prove customer retention. Base case credits no retention beyond one paid annual renewal. Free c-KOB reminders, the 2031 paper transition, incumbent portability and contract-specific data rights weaken lock-in; measure building retention, manager retention and routed-scope share separately (R03-S01, R03-S02, R03-S03, R03-S09, R03-S11).

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Contract-permitted, de-identified benchmarks for defect types, scope duration, first-pass protocol completeness, rework and partner reliability can improve routing and QA. No personal, raw KOB, protocol or photo reuse is assumed; supplier performance generated by the operator is the initial defensible dataset.
fingerprint.customer: Private professional property managers administering at least 100 housing-community, multifamily or small-commercial buildings concentrated in one Polish voivodeship; begin in Wielkopolska or Warsaw and exclude municipal tenders, national portfolios and one-off single-building buyers during validation.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Founder-led account-based sales to a hand-built list of 30 private managers with at least 100 buildings in one region, timed to real inspection calendars. Demand is counted only through paid pilots on the same terms. The family renewable installer may seed electrical-inspection supply and introductions but is not treated as proven buyer access.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A managed compliance desk, not a c-KOB replacement: normalize object/scope schedules, verify e-CRUB and insurance evidence, route regional partners, provide scope and protocol-completeness checklists, track defects and remediation status, and prepare manual or authorized-role c-KOB packets. The company performs no inspections, technical sign-off or remediation initially. Revenue is the recurring per-building fee plus the disclosed dispatch/QA fee; inspectors contract and invoice the building directly.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Only a manager whose written management agreement authorizes procurement signs the master service. Each building or community pays the signing inspector directly; the operating company invoices a test price of PLN 600 net per building at annual register setup or renewal plus a disclosed 15% coordination/QA fee only after an accepted protocol and c-KOB evidence packet. These are validation terms, not observed market prices.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A verified 12-month portfolio calendar shows annual, five-year, large-building or event-triggered controls coming due while scopes, qualified providers, prior defects and c-KOB/protocol handoffs are fragmented across files and vendors.

founder_fit: The founder's analytical and AI background fits schedule normalization, anomaly detection, structured protocol checks and operational measurement, and the no-camera preference is compatible with B2B account sales. The family's renewable installer can help test electrical-partner onboarding near Ostrów Wielkopolski. However, multi-specialty dispatch, May/November peaks, defect escalation and rework conflict with a solo founder's full-time job and preference against constant high-energy coordination. A pilot must remain one region, at most about 100 buildings and two or three partner firms until the two-hour-per-building operating ceiling is demonstrated.
risks: Protocol QA can be construed as technical assurance, creating liability beyond a software or coordination role.
Severe defects create urgent remediation, conflict and documentation obligations that overwhelm part-time coverage.
May and November peaks can concentrate scheduling failures and inspector scarcity.
Managers or communities can bypass the desk after the first introduction and contract inspectors directly.
Free c-KOB or incumbent product improvements can erase the remaining workflow differentiation.
A data incident involving resident, protocol or defect-photo information can create regulatory and reputational harm.
Low inspection ticket sizes make travel, rework, support and insurance allocation larger than the dispatch margin.
The founder may need an operations hire before revenue supports one, breaking the part-time and capital constraints.
thesis: Do not build a national inspector marketplace or another c-KOB calendar. A narrower, testable version is a one-region managed compliance desk that normalizes each portfolio's legally due scopes, routes already-qualified insured partners, checks packet completeness without replacing the signing inspector's technical judgment, and tracks defects. It is viable only if private managers pay a separate recurring fee, operational effort stays below two hours per building-year, and c-KOB can be handled through authorized/manual workflows.
title: Regional portfolio compliance desk for private managers with 100+ buildings
uncertainties: Whether two unrelated managers will pay the exact recurring and dispatch terms for at least 150 buildings.
Whether a manager can bind all buildings under one master agreement or needs per-community approvals.
Whether saved manager time or procurement/rework savings exceeds PLN 657 per building-year.
Whether coordination, QA and support stay at or below two hours per building-year with at least 95% first-pass packet completeness.
Whether three insured regional partners across required specialties accept service levels and economics.
Whether c-KOB supports any API or only role-based/manual work for this use case.
Whether contracts permit de-identified defect and performance benchmarks to be retained and reused.
Whether direct account acquisition can scale from one evidenced 415-object buyer to 70 100-building managers.
